summary: Cut at 7.1 in round 4. The scores so far: 6.3 in round 1, 6.7 in round 2, 7.0 in round 3 (cut), and 7.1 now. Caiman is 7.0 and the ship bar is 7.5. Every lost-wax gate is green, and I checked the export myself. finished-metal.stl has 1,403,596 triangles, 0 degenerate or zero-area faces, and every directed edge is matched by its reverse, so the mesh is closed and 2-manifold. Its minimum radius from the axis is 9.299999 mm against the 9.3 mm bore, and casting-pattern.stl matches it byte for byte after the header. Lost wax is Logan's recorded decision in the Moloch section of cataphracta.md, so the sand gates rightly do not apply. The extra round itself is not recorded anywhere in the repo; I have only the launching agent's word for it. It does not change the outcome, because the ring stays below 7.5 either way. Round 4 fixed the direction of the ripples. They now run round the ring, cover the whole crown, fork and end, and no longer read as diagonal wood grain. The feet now carry five splayed toes, and at 300 px the figure still reads as a thorny devil or horned lizard. But the fixes brought new faults, and old ones remain. (1) The new feet are flat cartoon hands with fat, rounded fingertips (stones.png, face.png). They read as a gecko, frog or glove, not as the thin clawed toes of Moloch. The outer toe curled over the edge stands off the cheek as a peg or nail stub in hero.png, side.png, reverse.png and shoulder.png, which a buyer will read as an unfinished sprue. The toes' thinnest section fell from 0.719 mm in round 3 to 0.175 mm, with 32.0 mm² under the floor. That fails round 3's own acceptance test (toes >= 0.6 mm), although land_widths names the section and gives its bench treatment. (2) The limbs still end in lumpy knob clusters at the wrist (face.png, upper-left; stones.png). (3) The ripples are regular, even-pitch zigzags that read as tyre tread or stylised water more than wind-blown sand. Their crests show crinkled, noisy highlights on the palm side (palm.png, right half; reverse.png). A polished gap of about 1.5-2.5 mm is still left between the ripples and the figure beside the upper hand and under the lower hand (face.png). (4) The tail still runs down the crown edge as a row of spikes pointing outward, and it reads as a spiked rail in reverse.png and hero.png. (5) Large polished domes remain under the mid-body cones, and the head carries a smooth round dome that reads as an eye in hero.png. Up close the head is a cluster of bubbles (stones.png). At 7.1 the ring edges past Caiman but sits below Basiliscus (7.2, cut) and well short of Arachne and Manticora (7.5). The verdict rules are unchanged, so it is cut.
strengths: At 300 px, with no caption, the figure reads as a thorny devil or horned lizard: a squat body, graded cones, a nuchal hump, splayed legs (hero-300, face-300).
The ripples now run round the ring, cover the whole crown with no seam, and fork and end (palm.png). The diagonal wood-grain read of round 3 is gone.
The graded cone field (22 major, 30 minor, 17 tail, 4 brow, 2 hump) gives the figure clear large, medium and small forms.
The silhouette is unlike anything in Cataphracta or on the Reptilia sheet: a figure crouched on the band, with the dorsal spines standing proud in side.png.
The engineering is clean. Every lost-wax gate is green, the closed mesh and pattern are independently verified, and every section under the 0.8 mm floor is named with its bench treatment.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: One subject throughout: a thorny devil on desert sand. The ripple band carries the theme round to the palm (palm.png), and nothing else competes with it.

checklist.item: The hide reads as this specific animal at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: hero-300 and face-300 read as a thorny devil or horned lizard. The new hands pull the read toward gecko or frog, but not far enough to lose it.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines that render crisp, with no combing, smearing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The ripple crests on the palm side show crinkled, noisy highlights (palm.png right half; reverse.png upper right). Up close the head is a bubble cluster with no crisp outline (stones.png). The toes are soft rounded blobs, and one runs over the edge like a drip (stones.png, bottom).

checklist.item: Stones sit in made settings and are visible
checklist.reason: No stones by design: 0 previewed and 0 reported. Not applicable.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: The body is sculpted, but the hands are flat cartoon cut-outs, and the curled outer toes stand off the cheeks as straight pegs (side.png, reverse.png, shoulder.png, hero.png lower right). Polished domes sit under the mid-body cones, and there is a round dome on the head (hero.png).

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: The bore-to-cheek and cheek-to-crown breaks survive in bare-vs-finished.png, side.png and hero.png.

checklist.item: A silhouette distinct from the other Cataphracta rings and from the Reptilia tiles
checklist.reason: It is the only ring with a figure crouched on the band. Nothing on the Reptilia sheet resembles it.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The figure matches Caiman's density. The ripples now cover the crown but at a single medium scale, with no small-scale grain, and the cheeks are bare polish. A 1.5-2.5 mm polished gap is still left around the figure (face.png). Overall the ring is roughly level with Caiman, not clearly above it.

punch_list.zone: Thorny devil part: all four feet ('toes', thinnest at 101.0 deg) and the curled outer toe on each foot
punch_list.change: Replace the cartoon-glove hands with Moloch feet. Each foot gets 5 slender, slightly curved toes, 1.2-1.6 mm long, 0.8 mm at the root tapering to 0.6 mm, each ending in a pointed 0.3 mm claw bead rather than a round pad. Toes 2-4 should be the longest. Delete the toe that curls over the edge: no toe may leave the crown or project off the cheek. Keep every toe fused along its full length.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png and face.png the feet read as clawed lizard feet, not a glove, frog or gecko. In side.png, reverse.png, shoulder.png and hero.png no peg, pin or drip stands off the cheek. In report.json land_widths toes thinnest_mm is >= 0.6 and under_floor_mm2 is <= 1.0.

punch_list.change: Break the regular zigzag. Vary the wavelength between 1.0 and 1.8 mm and the crest amplitude along each crest, and make the profile asymmetric: a gentle windward slope and a sharp lee crest. Add a secondary micro-ripple (0.3-0.4 mm wavelength, 0.04 mm high) in the troughs so the band has a small scale. Raise the alpha or mesh resolution on the palm side (about 200-340 deg) until the crest highlights run clean. Carry the ripples to within 0.8 mm of the figure's outline everywhere, including beside the upper and lower hands.
punch_list.acceptance: In palm.png and hero-300 a viewer says 'wind-blown sand', not tyre tread or water. In palm.png and reverse.png the crest highlights are continuous, with no crinkle. In face.png no polished gap wider than 1 mm touches the figure.

punch_list.zone: Limbs (thinnest at 87.4 deg): the wrist and ankle clusters
punch_list.change: Remove the knob clusters at each wrist and ankle. Taper the limb smoothly, from 1.2 mm at the shoulder to 0.8 mm at the wrist, into the foot, with 3-4 small cones along its top and no round lump over 0.6 mm across.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png and stones.png each limb is one continuous, tapering form into the foot, with no bubble cluster at the wrist.

punch_list.zone: Tail ('tail', thinnest at -31.6 deg, and the 'tail thorns')
punch_list.change: Turn the tail thorns to point up and back along the tail (at most 30 deg off the tail's own axis), not outward past the band edge. Keep the tail's outer edge within 0.5 mm of the crown edge and taper its tip to 0.8 mm.
punch_list.acceptance: In reverse.png and hero.png the tail reads as a tapering tail lying on the crown, and no row of spikes points outward along the cheek edge.

punch_list.zone: Major-thorn roots (mid-body, about 80-100 deg) and the head (about 115-125 deg)
punch_list.change: Sink the cone bases into the tubercle field with a 0.3 mm fillet, and replace the smooth domes with tubercles. On the head, flatten the smooth round dome and the bubble cluster into a small wedge with 4-6 flat, angular scales and the two brow horns.
punch_list.acceptance: In hero.png no polished dome over 1.0 mm sits under a cone, and nothing on the head reads as an eye. In stones.png the head reads as a wedge with scales, not a cluster of bubbles.
